items.headline: Motorcyclist, 25, and his 21-year-old pillion die in a Yio Chu Kang crash
items.summary: Police were alerted at about 3.35am on 25 June to a motorcycle that had self-skidded along Yio Chu Kang Road towards Upper Thomson. The 25-year-old male rider and his 21-year-old female pillion, believed to be a couple, were pronounced dead at the scene.

items.headline: Property agent jailed over an Australian scheme that cost investors S$16 million
items.summary: Licensed agent Wendy Kwek Siang Ling was jailed three months after pleading guilty under the Securities and Futures Act, as her company dealt in securities without an MAS licence. About 347 investors lost a total of S$16.21 million.

items.headline: Man gets a lifetime driving ban for a fourth drink-driving offence
items.summary: Kenny Yeap Beng Chye, 64, was sentenced to 10 months and six weeks' jail, fined S$26,000 and had his licence revoked for life after his fourth drink-driving conviction. He had drunk six to eight beers before crashing into a pillar in Tampines.

items.headline: HDB launches about 6,900 June BTO flats, including 2,520 with short waits
items.summary: HDB's June 2026 sales exercise offers around 6,900 flats, of which 2,520 have waiting times of about three years or less. These include Sembawang Portico (875 units, 2 years 7 months), Sembawang Brook (1,160 units) and Kebun Baru Ridge (485 units).

items.headline: Operation Sindhu winds down after evacuating 4,415 Indians from Iran and Israel
items.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs said Operation Sindhu brought home 4,415 nationals — 3,597 from Iran and 818 from Israel — on 19 special flights including three IAF C-17s, before being wound down on 26 June. Launched on 18 June, the operation also evacuated 14 OCI cardholders and several foreign nationals.

items.headline: India-China border trade resumes through the Lipulekh Pass after six years
items.summary: The first batch of 26 Indian traders is set to cross into Tibet through Uttarakhand's Lipulekh Pass on 26 June, resuming border trade halted since 2019-20. The reopening follows an August 2025 agreement to revive three Himalayan trade routes.

items.headline: Centre extends emergency powers to keep Tata's Mundra plant running on weak monsoon
items.summary: India invoked Section 11 of the Electricity Act to keep Tata Power's imported-coal Mundra plant operating through September, citing weak monsoon rains and the risk of power shortfalls during peak demand.

items.headline: Supreme Court to hear a plea against surrendering 152 Tamil Nadu medical seats
items.summary: A bench of Justices B.V. Nagarathna and Joymalya Bagchi issued notice to the Centre and Tamil Nadu on a plea by the state's Medical Officers Association opposing the surrender of 152 vacant super-speciality seats to the all-India quota for 2025-26.

items.headline: Update: UK breaks its June temperature record for a second straight day at 36.7C
items.summary: The UK provisionally set a new June maximum temperature record of 36.7C at Merryfield, Somerset, on 25 June, the second consecutive day the record fell and well above the 35.6C set in 1976. Wales recorded its hottest June day at 35.9C and Northern Ireland tied its June record at 30.8C.

items.headline: UK private sector shrinks for a second month as the flash PMI hits a 14-month low
items.summary: S&P Global's flash UK composite PMI slipped to 49.4 in June from 49.7 in May, a 14-month low and a second straight month below the 50 line dividing growth from contraction. Services led the decline, with firms citing Middle East energy costs on top of existing cost pressures.

items.headline: Resident doctors in England vote on a pay deal to end strikes, with the ballot closing today
items.summary: A BMA referendum on the government's offer — an average 6.6% pay uplift by April 2027 plus 4,500 new specialty training places — opened on 18 June and closes at noon on 26 June. A simple majority would settle the dispute; planned strikes on 15-19 June were called off pending the result.

items.headline: Met Office warns of thunderstorms, hail and flash flooding as the heatwave breaks
items.summary: After days of record heat, the Met Office issued thunderstorm warnings, with forecasters expecting frequent lightning, hail of 2-4cm and 30-50mm of rain in a few hours in places. There is a small chance of sudden flooding to homes and businesses as storms push north-eastwards.

items.headline: Twin earthquakes kill at least 188 in Venezuela as buildings collapse near Caracas
items.summary: A magnitude 7.2 quake struck west of Caracas on the evening of 24 June, followed 39 seconds later by a magnitude 7.5 quake, the strongest to hit Venezuela since 1900. At least 188 people were killed and 1,520 injured, and the government declared a state of emergency.

items.headline: Kenya arrests 355 as it marks two years since deadly Gen Z protests
items.summary: Police barricaded roads and detained people across Kenya on 25 June as families held memorials two years after anti-tax protests in which more than 120 people were killed. Interior Minister Kipchumba Murkomen said 355 were arrested nationwide, most in Nairobi and Kajiado.

items.headline: Iran's IRGC rejects a new Oman-IMO shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned on 25 June that vessels may use only Tehran-designated lanes through the Strait of Hormuz, rejecting a new corridor Oman said it had coordinated with the International Maritime Organization. The warning followed a tanker hugging Oman's coast and a ship attack that prompted the IMO to pause an evacuation of stranded vessels.

items.headline: A US-backed push to unify Libya's rival governments gains ground in the east
items.summary: A Washington initiative led by presidential adviser Massad Boulos to merge Libya's divided institutions has reportedly gained traction in the east, with foreign ministers from Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye meeting Boulos in Cairo. The plan is said to envisage Saddam Haftar leading a new presidential council.

items.headline: OpenAI unveils Jalapeno, its first custom AI chip, built with Broadcom
items.summary: OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled Jalapeno, OpenAI's first custom inference processor, co-developed from initial design to tape-out in about nine months. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said it offers roughly 50% cost savings versus typical AI GPUs, with initial deployment planned for late 2026.

items.headline: Ex-Infosys chief Vishal Sikka launches Hang Ten Systems with $32 million
items.summary: Vishal Sikka's new venture Hang Ten Systems raised a $32 million seed round led by Mayfield, with Aramco Ventures backing and Yahoo co-founder Jerry Yang on its board. The startup aims to take on the traditional IT-services industry, citing early customers including Siemens Gamesa and Fresenius.

items.headline: AI revenue outpaces data-center depreciation for a second straight quarter
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that global AI sales excluding China reached about $25 billion in the first quarter, edging past an estimated $21 billion in depreciation on chips and data centres. Depreciation still consumes more than two-thirds of AI revenue, underscoring the cost of the buildout.

items.headline: Robotics startup HaloBraid raises $7 million to speed up salon hair-braiding
items.summary: HaloBraid raised $7 million led by Alexis Ohanian's Seven Seven Six to launch its first device later this year, a robotic assistant designed to cut hours off salon braiding appointments.

items.headline: US Supreme Court shields Bayer from Roundup cancer-warning lawsuits
items.summary: The US Supreme Court ruled 7-2 on 25 June that federal pesticide law preempts state failure-to-warn claims, throwing out a $1.25 million verdict and curbing tens of thousands of Roundup suits. Bayer shares jumped as much as 20%.

items.headline: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge hits a three-year high as May PCE reaches 4.1%
items.summary: US headline PCE inflation accelerated to 4.1% year-on-year in May from 3.8% in April, the highest since 2023, with core PCE at 3.4%. The pickup, driven partly by higher oil prices, hardened expectations of a Federal Reserve rate increase later in 2026.

items.headline: Apple raises Mac and iPad prices as a memory-chip shortage bites
items.summary: Apple lifted prices on MacBooks and iPads by up to a few hundred dollars, with the entry MacBook now starting at $699, blaming surging memory costs; its shares fell about 5-6%. Microsoft followed by raising Xbox console prices by $100 to $150 from 1 August.

items.headline: Germany's Merck KGaA to buy Bio-Techne for $11.3 billion
items.summary: Merck KGaA agreed on 25 June to acquire US life-sciences toolmaker Bio-Techne for $73 a share in cash, valuing it at about $11.3 billion, a 36% premium and Merck's largest deal since buying Sigma-Aldrich in 2014. Bio-Techne shares jumped more than 20%.

items.headline: Qualcomm jumps 15% as it unveils Dragonfly data-center chips with Meta and Microsoft
items.summary: At its Investor Day on 24 June, Qualcomm launched its Dragonfly data-center line, including the C1000 CPU and AI300 accelerator, and named Meta and Microsoft as anchor customers, targeting $15 billion in data-center revenue by fiscal 2029.

items.headline: 🏎️ McLaren bring an upgraded rear wing to the Austrian GP, eyeing the top step
items.summary: McLaren confirmed an upgraded rear wing for this weekend's Austrian Grand Prix at the Red Bull Ring, where Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri scored a one-two last year. After Norris finished third last time out in Barcelona, the team believes a win is on at Spielberg.

items.headline: 🏎️ The Austrian GP weekend opens at the Red Bull Ring with Hamilton a title threat
items.summary: Formula 1's Austrian Grand Prix, the eighth round of the season, gets under way with first practice on 26 June. Lewis Hamilton arrives resurgent after his first Ferrari win last time out in Barcelona, closing on the championship leaders.

items.headline: 🎾 Jack Draper thrashes Diallo 6-1, 6-4 to reach the Eastbourne semi-finals
items.summary: Jack Draper beat Canada's Gabriel Diallo 6-1, 6-4 to reach the Eastbourne semi-finals, where he will face sixth seed Ugo Humbert. It is the British number one's best run of the season as he tunes up for Wimbledon.

items.headline: 🎾 Naomi Osaka reaches the Bad Homburg semi-finals with a 6-2, 6-2 win
items.summary: Naomi Osaka beat Ekaterina Alexandrova 6-2, 6-2 to reach the semi-finals at Bad Homburg, extending a strong grass-court run before Wimbledon.

items.headline: 🏏 Shafali's 53 lifts India past Bangladesh by five wickets to keep semis alive
items.summary: Shafali Verma made 53 off 34 balls as India chased down Bangladesh's 136 for 8, winning by five wickets at Old Trafford on 25 June. Radha Yadav took 3 for 28 to keep India second in Group 1 at the Women's T20 World Cup.

items.headline: AI screen turns up new antibiotics against drug-resistant gonorrhoea
items.summary: Researchers trained a deep-learning model on tens of thousands of molecules, then virtually screened about six million compounds to find new antibiotics against Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Two structurally novel candidates, MP20 and A1, killed the bacteria in mice and lab models without triggering resistance.

items.headline: Burnt bones push possible human fire use back to 1.79 million years ago
items.summary: Charred small-mammal bones found about 30 metres inside South Africa's Wonderwerk Cave, dated between 1.07 and 1.79 million years old, suggest early humans deliberately carried fire deep underground. The findings were published in PLOS One.

items.headline: Summer sun fails to fix a year-round vitamin D shortfall in at-risk Britons
items.summary: A Newcastle University study of nearly 300 people in northern Britain found vitamin D insufficiency in 54.8% of older adults and 72.1% of people from minoritised ethnic backgrounds, with no improvement over summer. The work appeared in the European Journal of Clinical Nutrition.

items.headline: Webb finds the first signs of salt clouds on a cold 'pink' world
items.summary: Astronomers used the James Webb Space Telescope to obtain the first spectrum of GJ 504b, a roughly 25-Jupiter-mass object about 57 light-years away, finding the best fit required salt clouds. It is the first direct evidence of such clouds on a cold companion.

fun_fact.headline: You are roughly half microbe by cell count
fun_fact.body: The human body contains roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells. A widely cited 2016 estimate put the figure at about 38 trillion bacteria to around 30 trillion human cells, so by cell count a person is nearly half microbe. Most of these bacteria live in the gut, where they help with digestion and shape the immune system.

puzzle.title: Hands of the Clock
puzzle.body:
At exactly 3:00, a clock's hour and minute hands are 90 degrees apart.
After 3:00, the minute hand catches up and the two hands point in exactly the same direction.

To the nearest second, at what time do the hour and minute hands overlap?
puzzle.approach: Think about how fast each hand turns and the gap it has to close.
puzzle.answer:
About 3:16:22 (more precisely, 3 hours, 16 minutes and 21 and 9/11 seconds).

The minute hand turns 6 degrees per minute and the hour hand 0.5 degrees per minute, so the minute hand gains 5.5 degrees every minute. At 3:00 it must close a 90-degree gap: 90 / 5.5 = 16.36... minutes, which is 16 minutes and about 21.8 seconds. So the hands overlap at roughly 3:16:22.

word_puzzle.title: Boxed In
word_puzzle.body:
A Letter Boxed square has three letters on each side. Connect letters to spell words: consecutive letters must come from different sides, and each new word must begin with the previous word's last letter. Use all 12 letters.

TOP:     W  Z  P
LEFT:    I  R  M
RIGHT:   A  U  G
BOTTOM:  D  L  N

Solve the whole box in just two words.
word_puzzle.approach: Find a long word, then a second word starting with its last letter, together using every letter.
word_puzzle.answer:
WIZARD → DUMPLING.

WIZARD ends in D, so the second word must start with D. DUMPLING does, and between them the two words use all twelve letters. No two consecutive letters ever sit on the same side of the box.
